intent.raw_query: Hawaii family beach vacation, $5000, 10 days, August 2026 from Seattle

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, shallow waters and equipment rentals on-site. An educational video about the reef ecosystem is shown before entry.

experiences.name: Luau Dinner at Old Lahaina Luau
experiences.description: Immerse your family in authentic Hawaiian culture with a traditional luau feast featuring kalua pig, poi, and fresh tropical fruits. Enjoy live hula performances, fire dancing, and storytelling that brings ancient Polynesian traditions to life. A memorable evening experience for the whole family.

experiences.name: Waimea Valley Hike and Waterfall Swim
experiences.description: Trek through a lush botanical garden along a family-friendly trail leading to the stunning 45-foot Waimea Falls. Kids will love swimming in the natural pool at the base of the waterfall. The valley also features cultural demonstrations and ancient Hawaiian archaeological sites along the path.

experiences.name: Surfing Lessons at Waikiki Beach
experiences.description: Take beginner surfing lessons with certified instructors on the gentle, rolling waves of Waikiki — considered the birthplace of modern surfing. Group lessons are ideal for families, and most beginners stand up on their first try. Boards and rash guards are included in the lesson fee.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Day Pass
experiences.description: Spend a full day exploring six authentic Polynesian village recreations representing Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and Aotearoa. Families can participate in hands-on cultural activities like coconut husking, spear throwing, and traditional weaving. The day concludes with a spectacular evening show featuring over 100 performers.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Hawaii
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - late night arrival at 22:30. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort Beachfront room and get settled.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at 22:30 via Flight UA. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort. Grab a light snack from a nearby convenience store or hotel vending machine. Rest and prepare for the days ahead.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or skip
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport food
meals.dinner: Quick convenience store snack near the resort (budget ~$5-10) or pack snacks from the mainland

day_by_day.notes: Late arrival day - no sightseeing planned. Pick up a local map and grab resort info at check-in. Set an early alarm to maximize Day 2. Look for a nearby grocery store or ABC Store to stock up on breakfast items to save money throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and take a sunrise walk along the beachfront directly from the resort. Enjoy the free natural beauty of the Hawaiian shoreline. Collect shells, dip your toes in the water, and take photos. This is completely free and one of Hawaii's best experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby local beach park (most are free public access). Set up with beach towels from the resort, swim, snorkel if you brought gear, and build sandcastles with the family. Look for a free public beach like a state beach park within walking or short driving distance of the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the beach - a quintessential Hawaii experience that costs nothing. Afterward, explore the immediate resort area and nearby streets for local flavor.

meals.breakfast: Grocery store haul - pick up fruit, yogurt, and juice from a nearby ABC Store or Foodland (~$10-15 for the family)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from the grocery store - sandwiches, chips, and fruit (~$15-20 for the family)
meals.dinner: Find a local plate lunch spot near the resort. Hawaiian plate lunches (rice, mac salad, protein) are filling and budget-friendly (~$8-12 per person)

day_by_day.notes: First full day - keep it relaxed and close to the resort. Visit a nearby grocery store in the morning to stock up on breakfast and snack items for the week. This will save significant money over 10 days. ABC Stores are conveniently located across Hawaii and carry affordable essentials.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local farmers market (many run on weekday and weekend mornings across Hawaii). Sample fresh tropical fruits like lychee, starfruit, and locally grown pineapple. Purchase affordable fresh produce for snacks throughout the week. Markets are free to browse and a wonderful cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a free or low-cost state or county beach park. Many Hawaiian beach parks offer free parking, restrooms, picnic tables, and lifeguards. Look for snorkeling spots with reef fish visible from shore. Bring or rent affordable snorkel gear to see Hawaii's colorful marine life up close.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through a nearby town or village. Browse local shops, watch street performers if available, and soak in the local atmosphere. Look for a food truck cluster for an affordable and delicious dinner.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit and pastries from the farmers market (~$8-12 for the family)
meals.lunch: Picnic at the beach park using groceries and farmers market finds (~$10-15 for the family)
meals.dinner: Food truck dinner - look for local favorites like garlic shrimp, kalua pork tacos, or poke bowls (~$10-15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Farmers markets in Hawaii typically run early morning (7am-noon). Check local listings for the nearest market to your resort. Food trucks are an iconic and budget-friendly Hawaii dining experience - look for clusters near beaches or town centers.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a free or low-admission botanical garden or nature preserve near your resort area. Hawaii's lush tropical flora is stunning and educational for families. Many botanical gardens offer free or reduced admission for children. Walk through native Hawaiian plant sections and learn about the islands' unique ecosystem.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a popular snorkeling beach. Hawaii's waters are teeming with sea turtles, tropical fish, and vibrant coral. Many of the best snorkeling spots in Hawaii are free public beaches. If you don't have gear, affordable rentals are available near most popular beaches ($10-15/day per set).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Enjoy a relaxing evening on the beach or resort grounds. Look for any free cultural performances or events happening nearby - many resorts and shopping centers host free hula or live music performances.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared at the resort using grocery store items - cereal, milk, fruit (~$5-8 for the family)
meals.lunch: Grab a shave ice and a quick bite from a local snack stand near the beach (~$10-15 for the family)
meals.dinner: Local diner or casual Hawaiian restaurant - look for early bird specials or keiki (kids) menus (~$12-18 per adult, kids often eat free or reduced)

day_by_day.notes: Sea turtle sightings are common at many Hawaiian beaches - remind children to observe from a distance and never touch. Check local event calendars for free cultural performances which are common at shopping centers and resort areas throughout Hawaii.

day_by_day.morning: Take a free or low-cost hike on a local trail. Hawaii has hundreds of hiking trails ranging from easy family-friendly walks to challenging treks. Look for a coastal trail or a short nature walk suitable for all ages. Many trailheads are free to access and offer spectacular ocean and mountain views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a free local cultural or historical site. Hawaii has numerous free historical parks, monuments, and cultural centers. Learn about Hawaiian history, the significance of the islands, and local traditions. Many sites have free self-guided tours with informational plaques.
day_by_day.evening: Beach bonfire (if permitted in your area) or evening beach walk. Check local regulations about beach fires. Alternatively, enjoy a quiet evening at the resort beachfront watching the stars - Hawaii's night skies are spectacular away from city lights.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared resort breakfast - toast, peanut butter, bananas (~$5 for the family)
meals.lunch: Pack trail snacks and sandwiches for the hike - trail mix, granola bars, PB&J (~$10 for the family)
meals.dinner: Local supermarket deli or poke counter - fresh poke bowls are affordable and authentically Hawaiian (~$10-14 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Always bring sunscreen, plenty of water, and appropriate footwear for hiking. Hawaii's sun is intense even on cloudy days. Check trail conditions before heading out - some trails may be closed due to rain or erosion. Poke from a supermarket deli counter is one of the best budget food values in Hawaii.

day_by_day.morning: Full beach morning at a different beach than previous days. Hawaii's beaches each have unique character - some are great for swimming, others for surfing or snorkeling. Research nearby beaches and try one with a different vibe. Build sandcastles, collect shells, and enjoy the warm Pacific waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Try a free or low-cost family beach activity. Look for free surf lessons or boogie board rentals from local community programs. Alternatively, join a free beach yoga class (many instructors offer free community classes on the beach). Or simply explore tide pools at a rocky beach section - fascinating for kids and free.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local shopping center or outdoor mall for window shopping and free entertainment. Many Hawaiian shopping centers feature free nightly entertainment including hula performances, live music, and cultural demonstrations. Great for families and completely free.

meals.breakfast: Acai bowl from a local cafe - a Hawaii staple that is filling and relatively affordable (~$8-12 per person)
meals.lunch: Beach picnic with groceries - wraps, fruit, chips, and cold drinks from a cooler (~$15-20 for the family)
meals.dinner: Local pizza or casual dining restaurant - look for family deals or combo specials (~$10-15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Mid-trip day - this is a good time to do laundry at the resort or a nearby laundromat to keep luggage manageable. Check in with the family on favorite activities and plan the remaining days accordingly. Restock groceries and snacks for the second half of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a free state or national park visitor center or museum. Hawaii has excellent free or low-cost educational facilities that teach about the islands' geology, ecology, and cultural history. Many national park sites have free admission on designated fee-free days - check the NPS website in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local neighborhood known for its character and charm. Walk through colorful streets, browse local boutiques and galleries (free to browse), and sample free tastings at local food shops. This gives an authentic feel for local Hawaiian life beyond the resort bubble.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset catamaran cruise or sunset beach viewing. Budget catamaran cruises can be found for $30-50 per person and are a magical family experience. Alternatively, find a well-known sunset viewing spot for a free but equally stunning experience.

meals.breakfast: Malasadas (Portuguese donuts) from a local bakery - a beloved Hawaii treat (~$1-2 each, get several for the family)
meals.lunch: Local ramen or noodle shop - Hawaii has excellent Asian-influenced noodle restaurants that are filling and affordable (~$10-14 per person)
meals.dinner: Celebrate the halfway point with a slightly splurge-worthy local restaurant - look for happy hour specials or early dinner deals (~$15-20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 marks the halfway point of the trip. Consider splurging slightly on a sunset cruise if budget allows - it is a memorable family experience. Check for discount coupon books available at the resort front desk or visitor information centers, which often have BOGO deals on activities and restaurants.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to a famous or scenic lookout point. Hawaii has spectacular panoramic viewpoints that are free to access. Arrive early to beat crowds and enjoy the cooler morning temperatures. Take family photos with the stunning backdrop of ocean, mountains, or valleys.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a free or low-cost waterfall or natural attraction. Many of Hawaii's most beautiful waterfalls are accessible via short hikes and are completely free. Pack a picnic and spend the afternoon in a lush valley or rainforest setting - a beautiful contrast to the beach days.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the beach for one last evening swim before the final days of the trip. Enjoy a relaxed dinner and early evening to rest up for the remaining adventures.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared at resort - eggs, toast, fruit (~$5-8 for the family)
meals.lunch: Picnic at the waterfall or natural attraction - sandwiches and snacks packed from the resort (~$10-15 for the family)
meals.dinner: Casual beachside restaurant or grill - look for fish tacos, burgers, or local specials (~$12-16 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Waterfall trails can be slippery - wear appropriate footwear and supervise children carefully near water. Always stay on marked trails and observe any posted warnings. Bring insect repellent for rainforest areas. The contrast between beach and rainforest environments is one of Hawaii's most unique features.

day_by_day.morning: Final major activity day - revisit your family's favorite beach or activity from the trip. Let the kids choose their favorite spot for a special last full day of activities. Spend a leisurely morning enjoying the beach, swimming, and soaking in the Hawaiian atmosphere one more time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Souvenir shopping on a budget. Visit local markets, ABC Stores, or outlet areas for affordable Hawaiian souvenirs. Look for locally made items like macadamia nuts, Hawaiian sea salt, or small koa wood items. Set a per-person souvenir budget to keep spending in check. Avoid resort gift shops which tend to be overpriced.
day_by_day.evening: Special farewell dinner at a local Hawaiian restaurant. Splurge slightly for a memorable final dinner - try traditional Hawaiian foods like poi, laulau, kalua pig, or haupia dessert. This is a great opportunity to experience authentic Hawaiian cuisine as a family.

meals.breakfast: Special treat breakfast - local pancake house or breakfast diner for a memorable morning meal (~$10-15 per person)
meals.lunch: Light lunch while souvenir shopping - grab a quick bite from a food court or casual eatery (~$8-12 per person)
meals.dinner: Traditional Hawaiian plate lunch restaurant or local Hawaiian cuisine spot for a farewell feast (~$15-25 per person for a special final night)

day_by_day.notes: Best souvenir value tips: macadamia nuts in bulk at Costco or grocery stores, local honey, Hawaiian sea salt, and Kona coffee are all excellent and affordable. Avoid buying anything labeled Made in China at tourist shops. Local farmers markets often have the best prices on authentic Hawaiian goods.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk on the beach - a peaceful and free farewell to Hawaii. Take last photos, collect a few shells as free souvenirs, and say goodbye to the ocean. Pack up the room and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort according to check-out time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time, explore any last-minute sights near the airport or resort area. Visit a final lookout or scenic spot on the way to the airport. Allow plenty of time for airport check-in, security, and any last-minute duty-free shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Hawaii with wonderful family memories. The airport has food options for a final meal in paradise before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Use up remaining grocery store items for a final resort breakfast - finish off any food purchased during the trip (~$5 or less using existing supplies)
meals.lunch: Light meal near the airport or at the airport - look for local options like a plate lunch counter (~$10-15 per person)
meals.dinner: Airport dining before departure or on the plane (~$10-20 per person depending on flight time)

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11am - confirm with the resort. Allow at least 2.5-3 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security. Use up any remaining local currency or gift cards before departing. Consider donating any leftover non-perishable food items to a local food bank or leaving for resort housekeeping staff as a kind gesture.

trip_options.title: Classic Hawaii Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Daniel K. Inouye International Airport at 22:30. Collect luggage, arrange ground transportation (shuttle or rideshare ~$20–35), and check in to Aegean Bliss Resort. Settle into your beachfront room and unwind with a light snack.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or airport grab-and-go
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport food court
meals.dinner: Late-night snack from a 24-hour ABC Store or hotel vending — keep it simple after a long travel day

day_by_day.notes: Do not schedule any activities today. Focus entirely on a smooth arrival and rest. Confirm resort check-in details in advance since arrival is after 10 PM. Pack a carry-on snack bag for the kids to avoid hunger meltdowns upon landing.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely resort breakfast. Take a relaxed first walk along the beachfront to get your bearings. Let the kids splash in the resort pool or wade in the ocean shallows — no agenda, just decompression.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Waikiki Beach for your first real Hawaiian beach experience. Rent beach chairs and an umbrella (~$20–30), build sandcastles, swim in the calm surf, and browse the beachside shops along Kalakaua Avenue.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Kalakaua Avenue for dinner and enjoy the lively Waikiki atmosphere. Watch the free hula and music performances at Kuhio Beach Hula Mound (free, nightly around sunset).

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — fuel up for the day
meals.lunch: Romy's Kahuku Prawns & Shrimp or a casual beachside café near Waikiki (~$15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Duke's Waikiki — iconic oceanfront restaurant with mid-range Hawaiian plates, great for families (~$25–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is a gentle reorientation day. Don't overbook — jet lag may still be a factor, especially for children. Apply reef-safe sunscreen throughout the day. Pick up a reusable water bottle and snacks at a nearby Foodland or ABC Store.

day_by_day.morning: Surfing Lessons at Waikiki Beach — Book a 2-hour beginner group lesson with certified instructors on the gentle rolling waves of Waikiki. This is one of the best places in the world to learn to surf and is ideal for all family members ages 5+. Equipment is included (~$60–80 per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: Recover from the morning workout at the resort pool or beach. Grab shave ice from a nearby stand — try Matsumoto's or Island Snow for a classic Hawaiian treat. Walk through Kapiolani Park and visit the Honolulu Zoo (~$20 adults, $14 kids) for a low-key family afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Ala Moana Center for dinner and some light shopping. This is one of the largest open-air malls in the world and has great family dining options.

meals.breakfast: Cinnamon's Restaurant in Kailua — famous for their Hawaiian-style pancakes and eggs (~$15–20 per person)
meals.lunch: Beachside shave ice + plate lunch from a local food truck near Waikiki (~$12–18 per person)
meals.dinner: Panda Express or California Pizza Kitchen at Ala Moana for a relaxed, budget-friendly family dinner (~$15–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book surf lessons in advance online to secure your preferred time slot. Children should be comfortable in the water. Bring a change of dry clothes for after the lesson. Sunscreen is essential — the Hawaiian sun is intense even on cloudy days.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — One of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries. Arrive early (doors open at 6:45 AM) to beat the crowds and secure parking. Watch the mandatory 9-minute marine education video, then snorkel in crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and sea turtles. Entry is $25 per adult, free for kids under 13.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive the scenic Makapuu Lighthouse Trail (easy 2-mile round trip paved path) for panoramic ocean views. Afterward, stop at Halona Blowhole Lookout and Sandy Beach for dramatic coastal scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort, shower, and enjoy a relaxed evening. Visit the hotel bar or lounge for sunset cocktails (mocktails for kids) overlooking the ocean.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort or grab malasadas (Portuguese donuts) from Leonard's Bakery on the way (~$1–2 each)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snacks at Hanauma Bay (outside food is allowed in the picnic area) — pick up supplies from a grocery store the night before
meals.dinner: Ono Seafood — a beloved local hole-in-the-wall famous for fresh poke bowls (~$15–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations made online — book 2 days ahead as spots fill up fast. Bring your own snorkel gear or rent on-site (~$12). Do not touch the coral or marine life. Parking is $3. Arrive no later than 7:15 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Polynesian Cultural Center Day Pass — Spend the full day exploring six authentic Polynesian village recreations representing Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and Aotearoa. Morning is perfect for village tours, canoe rides, and interactive cultural demonstrations. Day passes start at ~$60 per adult, $48 per child.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Polynesian Cultural Center — catch live performances, try traditional foods at the marketplace, and participate in hands-on activities like fire-making, spear throwing, and weaving. The center is located in Laie on the North Shore (~45 min from Waikiki).
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the spectacular 'HA: Breath of Life' evening show — a world-class theatrical Polynesian performance with stunning costumes and lighting (included in most packages or add-on ~$20). Dinner package available on-site.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the resort before the drive north
meals.lunch: Gateway Buffet inside the Polynesian Cultural Center — all-you-can-eat Hawaiian and Polynesian dishes (~$30 per adult, included in some packages)
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau Dinner Package at the Polynesian Cultural Center OR dine at Hukilau Café in Laie on the way back (~$20–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase tickets online in advance for best pricing and to avoid sellouts. The center is about 45 minutes from Waikiki — plan for traffic. Comfortable walking shoes are essential. The full day pass with evening show is the best value. Allow 8–10 hours total.

day_by_day.morning: Waimea Valley Hike and Waterfall Swim — Trek through a lush botanical garden along a family-friendly 1.5-mile trail leading to the stunning 45-foot Waimea Falls. The trail is paved and suitable for all ages. Life jackets are provided for swimming in the pool below the waterfall. Entry is ~$20 adults, $10 kids.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hike, head to Waimea Bay Beach Park just down the road — one of Oahu's most beautiful beaches with calm summer waters perfect for swimming and snorkeling. In summer the waves are gentle, making it ideal for families.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Honolulu and stop at a famous North Shore shrimp truck for dinner. Giovanni's or Romy's are iconic stops beloved by locals and visitors alike.

meals.breakfast: Sunrise Café or Kono's in Haleiwa — try the breakfast burritos (~$10–15 per person)
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at Waimea Bay or grab plate lunches from Haleiwa Joe's Haiku Gardens (~$15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck in Kahuku — famous garlic shrimp plates (~$15–18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Waimea Valley opens at 9 AM. Bring water shoes for the waterfall swim and a change of clothes. The North Shore has a very different, laid-back vibe from Waikiki — enjoy the slower pace. Haleiwa town is charming for a quick browse of local boutiques and galleries.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Pearl Harbor — A profound and important historical experience for the whole family. Book advance tickets for the USS Arizona Memorial and USS Missouri Battleship tour (~$30–60 per person depending on packages). The visitor center and museum are free. Allow 3–4 hours minimum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Aloha Tower Marketplace at Honolulu Harbor for lunch and a stroll. Explore the historic downtown Honolulu area, visit the Iolani Palace (the only royal palace on US soil, ~$22 adults), and walk through the State Capitol grounds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a relaxed beach evening. Enjoy a bonfire or stargazing on the beach if available, or take a sunset swim. Treat the family to ice cream at a nearby parlor.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before heading to Pearl Harbor
meals.lunch: Gordon Biersch Brewery Restaurant at Aloha Tower Marketplace — good burgers, salads, and local dishes (~$20–30 per person)
meals.dinner: Helena's Hawaiian Food in Kalihi — a James Beard Award-winning local institution for authentic Hawaiian cuisine (~$15–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor is one of the most visited sites in Hawaii — book tickets weeks in advance. No bags larger than a small purse are allowed inside (free storage available). The experience can be emotionally heavy for younger children; preview the history beforehand. Arrive early to avoid long lines.

day_by_day.morning: Luau Dinner at Old Lahaina Luau (Note: If visiting Maui is not part of the itinerary, substitute with a Honolulu-based luau such as the Paradise Cove Luau on Oahu). Paradise Cove Luau is located 27 miles from Waikiki and offers an authentic experience with imu ceremony, traditional games, and a buffet feast (~$115 adults, $75 kids). Spend the morning relaxing at the resort beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy a leisurely afternoon at the resort — use the pool, do some light beachcombing, or rent kayaks or paddleboards from the resort beach (~$25–40/hour). This is a great low-key afternoon before the big luau evening.
day_by_day.evening: Paradise Cove Luau — Arrive at 5 PM for pre-show activities including lei making, coconut husking, and traditional games. The main luau show begins at sunset with hula dancing, fire knife performance, and a traditional kalua pig feast. Transportation can be arranged from Waikiki (~$15–20 round trip).

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or Eggs 'n Things — a Waikiki institution known for their enormous pancakes (~$15–20 per person)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort pool bar — sandwiches, salads, and tropical drinks (~$15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Full buffet feast included at Paradise Cove Luau — kalua pig, poi, haupia, lomi salmon, and more

day_by_day.notes: Book luau tickets at least 1–2 weeks in advance. Old Lahaina Luau is on Maui — if staying exclusively on Oahu, Paradise Cove is the top equivalent alternative. Dress in aloha attire (floral shirts, sundresses) for the full experience. Mosquito repellent is recommended for the outdoor evening event.

day_by_day.morning: Diamond Head Crater Hike — An iconic Honolulu landmark. The 1.6-mile round trip trail climbs to the 760-foot summit with panoramic views of Waikiki and the Pacific. The hike takes about 1.5–2 hours and is suitable for older children. Entry is $5 per person. Arrive early (7 AM) to avoid heat and crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reward yourselves with a visit to Kaimana Beach (also known as Sans Souci Beach) — a quieter, locals-favorite beach just east of Waikiki with calm, clear waters and great snorkeling near the reef. Spend the afternoon swimming, relaxing, and enjoying the less crowded atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Final big family dinner in Waikiki. Explore the International Marketplace food hall or treat the family to a nicer sit-down restaurant for a memorable last full evening out.

meals.breakfast: Grab malasadas and coffee from Leonard's Bakery on the way to Diamond Head (~$5–10)
meals.lunch: Barefoot Beach Café at Kaimana Beach — casual, affordable, right on the sand (~$15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Orchids at Halekulani Hotel — upscale beachfront dining for a special family dinner (~$45–65 per person) OR Roy's Waikiki for Hawaiian fusion (~$35–50 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head requires advance reservations online — walk-ins are not guaranteed. Bring plenty of water, sunscreen, and closed-toe shoes for the hike. The summit stairs include a dark tunnel section — bring a small flashlight. This is a great photography day with stunning views.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for one final sunrise walk on the beach — soak in the last moments of Hawaii. Pack up your belongings and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. If time allows, take a final dip in the ocean or pool before departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time: Visit the Ala Moana Center for last-minute souvenir shopping (Honolulu Cookie Company, Longs Drugs for local treats, local boutiques). Pick up Hawaiian coffee, macadamia nuts, and chocolate-covered treats to bring home.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Daniel K. Inouye International Airport. Allow 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in, security, and boarding. Reflect on an incredible 10 days in paradise.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast or a quick stop at Liliha Bakery for coco puffs and breakfast plates (~$10–15 per person)
meals.lunch: Mariposa at Neiman Marcus in Ala Moana (splurge-worthy farewell lunch with ocean views, ~$30–40 per person) OR food court at Ala Moana (~$15 per person)
meals.dinner: Airport dining at HNL — Island Brew Coffeehouse & Kitchen or Panda Express for a casual pre-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Confirm flight departure time and arrange transportation to the airport in advance (rideshare, shuttle, or taxi ~$25–40). Leave extra time for traffic — Honolulu traffic can be unpredictable. Check airline baggage policies if you've purchased souvenirs. Mahalo for an amazing family trip to Hawaii!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Hawaii Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, shallow waters and equipment rentals on-site. An educational video about the reef ecosystem is shown before entry.

experiences.name: Luau Dinner at Old Lahaina Luau
experiences.description: Immerse your family in authentic Hawaiian culture with a traditional luau feast featuring kalua pig, poi, and fresh tropical fruits. Enjoy live hula performances, fire dancing, and storytelling that brings ancient Polynesian traditions to life. A memorable evening experience for the whole family.

experiences.name: Waimea Valley Hike and Waterfall Swim
experiences.description: Trek through a lush botanical garden along a family-friendly trail leading to the stunning 45-foot Waimea Falls. Kids will love swimming in the natural pool at the base of the waterfall. The valley also features cultural demonstrations and ancient Hawaiian archaeological sites along the path.

experiences.name: Surfing Lessons at Waikiki Beach
experiences.description: Take beginner surfing lessons with certified instructors on the gentle, rolling waves of Waikiki — considered the birthplace of modern surfing. Group lessons are ideal for families, and most beginners stand up on their first try. Boards and rash guards are included in the lesson fee.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Day Pass
experiences.description: Spend a full day exploring six authentic Polynesian village recreations representing Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and Aotearoa. Families can participate in hands-on cultural activities like coconut husking, spear throwing, and traditional weaving. The day concludes with a spectacular evening show featuring over 100 performers.

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Honolulu Airport at 22:30 via United Airlines. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in to your Beachfront suite, enjoy a welcome amenity (chilled champagne and tropical fruit platter prepared by the resort). Light unpacking and settle in.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or airport dining
meals.lunch: In-flight or airport dining
meals.dinner: Late-night room service at Aegean Bliss Resort — order the resort's signature Hawaiian poke bowl and grilled mahi-mahi with a glass of local wine

day_by_day.notes: Request early check-in or a guaranteed room hold in advance given the late arrival. Confirm private airport transfer with the concierge prior to departure from home. Keep luggage light for carry-on to expedite exit from the airport.

day_by_day.morning: Slow start — enjoy a leisurely resort breakfast on your private beachfront terrace. After breakfast, take a relaxed stroll along the resort's private beach, acclimate to the Hawaiian sun, and let the family decompress from travel. Optional: dip in the resort's infinity pool.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Waikiki Beach for beginner Surfing Lessons with certified instructors. The gentle rolling waves make this ideal for all family members including children. Lessons typically run 90 minutes and include all equipment. Post-lesson, enjoy shave ice from a nearby premium vendor.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for sunset cocktails at the beachfront bar. Dress for a premium dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant — enjoy fresh island seafood, locally sourced produce, and stunning ocean views.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort beachfront breakfast — fresh tropical fruits, eggs Benedict with lomi salmon, Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Beachside light bites at Waikiki — Nobu Honolulu for a premium Japanese-Hawaiian fusion lunch
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort signature restaurant — Chef's tasting menu featuring local catch, Wagyu beef, and Hawaiian dessert selections

day_by_day.notes: Book surfing lessons in advance through the resort concierge. Apply reef-safe sunscreen — required at most Hawaii beaches. This is an intentionally lighter day to ease into the trip after late arrival the night before.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Hanauma Bay for Snorkeling. Arrive before 8:00 AM to secure entry (reservations required — book in advance). Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish, sea turtles, and vibrant coral. Snorkel gear rental available on-site or bring premium gear from the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a midday break and poolside lunch. In the afternoon, treat the family to a private luxury catamaran sunset cruise booked through the resort concierge — includes snorkeling stops, onboard refreshments, and stunning coastline views.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the Luau Dinner at Old Lahaina Luau (note: Old Lahaina Luau is on Maui — coordinate with concierge for inter-island logistics or select a premium Oahu luau alternative such as Paradise Cove Luau). Immerse in authentic Hawaiian culture with kalua pig, poi, hula dancing, and fire knife performances.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — acai bowls, macadamia nut pancakes, fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Poolside luxury — grilled fish tacos, lobster sliders, and tropical smoothies at the resort pool bar
meals.dinner: Traditional Hawaiian luau feast — kalua pig, laulau, haupia coconut pudding, and tropical cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance online reservations — book as early as possible as slots fill up weeks ahead. Confirm luau booking and transportation at least 2 weeks before the trip. Bring waterproof camera or underwater phone case for snorkeling.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day experience at the Polynesian Cultural Center. Depart after a hearty breakfast. Spend the morning exploring six authentic Polynesian village recreations representing Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and Aotearoa. Participate in hands-on cultural activities — fire-making, coconut husking, and traditional crafts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Polynesian Cultural Center — enjoy the afternoon canoe pageant on the lagoon, watch cultural performances, and explore the IMAX theater. Premium Ali'i Luau package recommended for an elevated dining and show experience.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the spectacular Ha: Breath of Life evening show at the Polynesian Cultural Center — a world-class theatrical performance featuring over 100 performers. Return to the resort by private transfer.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — eggs your way, fresh-baked pastries, tropical fruit platters, Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Polynesian Cultural Center — Gateway Restaurant buffet featuring island-inspired dishes from across Polynesia
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau premium dinner package at the Polynesian Cultural Center — includes reserved seating, premium menu, and full show access

day_by_day.notes: Purchase the premium Ambassador Package for the Polynesian Cultural Center for the best family experience — includes priority seating, guided tours, and exclusive backstage access. The center is approximately 35 miles from Waikiki — arrange private luxury transport through the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private family helicopter tour of Oahu's most dramatic landscapes — fly over Diamond Head, the Ko'olau Mountains, Waimea Valley, and the North Shore. This 60–90 minute premium experience offers unparalleled aerial views and makes for unforgettable family memories.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Waimea Valley for the Hike and Waterfall Swim. Trek through a lush botanical garden along a family-friendly 1.5-mile trail leading to the stunning 45-foot Waimea Falls. Swim in the natural pool beneath the falls — lifeguards on duty. Explore the valley's diverse tropical plant collections along the way.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a relaxing evening. Book a private in-suite family spa experience — massages, facials, and hydrotherapy treatments tailored for all ages. Enjoy a quiet dinner at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — smoothie bowls, avocado toast with fresh crab, Kona espresso
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet lunch prepared by the resort kitchen — packed in a premium basket for Waimea Valley; includes artisan sandwiches, tropical fruits, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Resort fine dining — pan-seared opah fish, truffle risotto, and a shared chocolate lava cake dessert

day_by_day.notes: Book the helicopter tour well in advance — Blue Hawaiian Helicopters or Sunshine Helicopters offer premium private tours. Waimea Valley requires water shoes for the waterfall swim — available at the resort gift shop. Spa bookings should be made at least 3 days in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning at the resort's private beach — build sandcastles, kayak, paddleboard, or simply relax under a private cabana with butler service. This is a designated rest and recharge morning for the family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private snorkeling tour with a luxury charter company — explore less-crowded reef systems along Oahu's coastline with a private guide. Spot Hawaiian green sea turtles, colorful reef fish, and vibrant coral formations. Includes premium snorkel equipment, flotation devices for children, and onboard refreshments.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Iolani Palace and downtown Honolulu for a sunset cultural stroll (if open in the evening) or explore the vibrant nightlife of the Chinatown arts district. Enjoy a premium farm-to-table dinner at one of Honolulu's top-rated restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Cabana breakfast service on the resort's private beach — fresh pastries, tropical juices, and a full hot breakfast delivered to your loungers
meals.lunch: Onboard the charter boat — catered gourmet spread with fresh poke, sushi rolls, charcuterie, and chilled beverages
meals.dinner: MW Restaurant Honolulu — award-winning contemporary Hawaiian cuisine featuring locally sourced ingredients and creative island flavors

day_by_day.notes: Confirm private snorkel charter at least one week in advance. MW Restaurant is one of Honolulu's most acclaimed dining destinations — reservations should be made well ahead of time. Request a window or terrace table for ambiance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Pearl Harbor National Memorial for a meaningful and educational family experience. Tour the USS Arizona Memorial, USS Missouri Battleship, and the Pacific Aviation Museum. Book the premium guided tour for priority access and expert narration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a poolside afternoon. Enjoy resort amenities — waterslide (if available), snorkeling in the lagoon, beach volleyball, or a family cooking class offered by the resort's executive chef featuring traditional Hawaiian dishes.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner cruise aboard a luxury catamaran — includes a premium catered dinner, open bar, live Hawaiian music, and spectacular views of Diamond Head and the Honolulu skyline at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — loco moco (premium wagyu beef version), fresh papaya, macadamia nut granola
meals.lunch: Pearl Harbor area — Navatek Cruises café or a premium nearby restaurant; fresh island salads and grilled fish
meals.dinner: Luxury sunset dinner cruise — multi-course catered meal with fresh seafood, tropical cocktails, and dessert under the stars

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor requires advance reservations — book the premium tour package for skip-the-line access and private guide. The memorial can be emotionally intense for younger children — prepare them with age-appropriate context beforehand. Sunset cruise departs from Honolulu Harbor — confirm pickup time with operator.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the scenic Windward Coast — stop at the Nuuanu Pali Lookout for breathtaking panoramic views of the Ko'olau cliffs and windward valleys. Continue to Kailua Beach, consistently rated one of the world's best beaches, for a morning of swimming, kayaking, and paddleboarding in turquoise waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming Kailua town — browse local boutiques, art galleries, and specialty food shops. Visit Lanikai Beach for an afternoon swim in its impossibly calm, clear waters. Optional: kayak to the Mokulua Islands (the 'Mokes') with a private guide.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a private beachfire experience arranged by the concierge — roast marshmallows, watch the stars, and enjoy a curated cheese and charcuterie board with Hawaiian wines and craft cocktails on your private beach.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — eggs Benedict with kalua pork, fresh mango, Kona cold brew
meals.lunch: Kailua town — Kalapawai Market for premium gourmet sandwiches, salads, and locally sourced provisions; enjoy as a picnic on Kailua Beach
meals.dinner: In-suite or private beachside dining experience arranged by the resort — seared ahi tuna, grilled lobster, and tropical desserts served under the stars

day_by_day.notes: Kailua Beach parking can be limited — arrange a private driver or rideshare. Lanikai kayak rentals are available through local outfitters — book in advance. The private beachfire experience should be arranged with the resort concierge at least 2 days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning whale watching or dolphin encounter cruise (seasonal — check operator availability for August). Alternatively, enjoy a private stand-up paddleboard yoga session on the calm morning ocean waters arranged through the resort. A peaceful, rejuvenating family experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Diamond Head State Monument for a hike to the summit crater — a moderate 1.6-mile round trip with rewarding panoramic views of Waikiki and the Pacific Ocean. Family-friendly with younger children. Follow with a visit to Kapiolani Park for a relaxing picnic and lawn games.
day_by_day.evening: Final full-evening luxury dinner at one of Honolulu's premier fine-dining establishments. Reflect on the trip over an exceptional meal, share favorite memories, and toast to the journey.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full spread; indulge in the resort's signature dishes one more time before the final full day
meals.lunch: Kapiolani Park picnic — gourmet provisions from a premium Honolulu deli or catered basket from the resort
meals.dinner: Senia Restaurant Honolulu — James Beard Award-nominated chef, innovative tasting menu blending global techniques with Hawaiian ingredients; reserve the chef's table for a premium interactive experience

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head requires advance reservations for entry — book online before the trip. Start the hike early to avoid midday heat. Senia Restaurant is one of Honolulu's most sought-after reservations — book as early as possible, ideally 30+ days in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise on the private beach — wake early to watch the sun rise over the Pacific from your beachfront suite. Enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at the resort. Complete packing and check-out formalities. Store luggage with the concierge if the flight is in the afternoon or evening.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time — final swim at the resort pool or beach, last-minute souvenir shopping at premium local boutiques or the resort gift shop (Koa wood items, Hawaiian sea salt, macadamia nut collections, and local art make excellent gifts). Resort spa for a final relaxing treatment if time allows.
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury transfer to Honolulu International Airport. Depart Hawaii with extraordinary memories of a world-class family adventure.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — choose your favorites from the week; order the full spread as a celebratory send-off
meals.lunch: Resort poolside or a farewell meal at the resort's casual beachside café — fresh fish, tropical smoothies, and coconut desserts
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or onboard flight meal (request premium meal option when booking)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time and late checkout options with the resort — a 2:00 PM checkout may be available for premium guests. Arrange airport transfer at least 3 hours before departure. Pack any perishable Hawaiian food items (such as fresh poke or fruit) in checked luggage with ice packs or ship them home via a local specialty service. Mahalo for an incredible journey!
